Disabled by default (enabled: false) for backward compatibility. Preferred: store this block in ~/.config/kyoro/synthesis_panel.json instead — it takes precedence over this inline value and keeps model choices out of the versioned config.

_device_registry_note: List the devices you actually own. Each entry needs a unique device_id; sensor_type is used by importers and source_priority to disambiguate metrics. Valid sensor_type: optical_wrist | optical_wrist_gps | chest_strap | handheld_ecg | ring | handheld_gps | scale | bp_monitor | glucometer | thermometer | smartphone | phone_optical | cgm | hub | weather_station. Add date_to for retired devices. serial is required for Polar wrist devices so import_polar.py can automatically identify which watches recorded H7/H10 chest-strap RR intervals; leave null for non-Polar or chest-strap devices. Optional 'regulatory' block documents regulatory status; grade: 'medical' | 'research_grade' | 'consumer'. IVD devices (CGM, glucometer) use ivdr_class instead of mdr_class. Optional 'source_apps' (list of strings): every source_app value this device's data can appear under in measurements/sessions — matters when the same physical device is reachable via more than one import path (e.g. a PDF export and an app-screenshot import of the same reading get two different source_app values). Only needed if you reference this device_id in clinical.reference_devices; compute_calibrate_sources.py uses it to resolve which source_app rows belong to your configured calibration anchor.

clinical._reference_devices_note: Optional: per-metric calibration/reference device_id (must exist in device_registry above). Unset metrics fall back to the project's hardcoded default anchor (see compute_calibrate_sources.py ANCHORS, compute_pem.py's HRV source hierarchy) — leaving this empty changes nothing. For compute_calibrate_sources.py to resolve a configured device into an anchor, that device_registry entry also needs 'source_apps' set (see _device_registry_note above); without it, that metric still falls back to the hardcoded default.
clinical._measured_at_note: Optional: formally measured aerobic/anaerobic threshold in bpm — from cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPET/VT1) or a graded lactate test (LT1), ideally with a provider experienced in ME/CFS/PEM pacing (standard maximal-effort protocols risk triggering a crash). Set measured_at_bpm (the threshold in bpm), measured_at_date (YYYY-MM-DD), and measured_at_method ('cpet' or 'lactate'). When set, compute_pem.py's aerobic-threshold trigger (Config.measured_at_bpm) uses this directly instead of the HRV-derived DFA-alpha1 HRVT1 estimate, whose reliability is not established under autonomic dysfunction (see compute_pem.py comment near _HRVT1_MIN_MARGIN).
clinical._pacing_note: Optional: compute_hr_zones.py zone boundaries for pacing/exertion-budget scoring. Add a 'pacing' object here (sibling of this note, e.g. 'pacing': {'zone_thresholds_bpm': [..4 values..], 'zone_weights': [..5 values..]}) to override the default. zone_thresholds_bpm needs exactly 4 absolute bpm values (the boundaries between the 5 zones: recovery < z1 | z1-z2 | z2-z3 | z3-z4 | red zone >= z4) — ideally taken from a lactate/exercise test's aerobic and anaerobic thresholds. zone_weights needs exactly 5 entries (one per zone) and controls how disproportionately higher zones count toward the daily budget. Left unset here deliberately: without this block, thresholds fall back to fixed percentages of max_hr (or the 220-age rule of thumb if max_hr is also unset) — a reasonable generic default, whereas a copied-in example bpm value would silently override that personalized fallback with a number that isn't actually yours.
clinical._baseline_note: compute_personal_baseline.py device filter. baseline_method: all_iqr | all_top | device_iqr | device_top. baseline_device: list of device_ids to restrict device_top/device_iqr to (your own wrist-device history, e.g. which watch you wore when) — empty = no filter, all devices count.
clinical._observations_note: Clinical observations not derivable from wearable data alone. Used by analyse_clinical_addendum.py to supplement the data-only synthesis with pharmacological response patterns and known methodological test limitations.

treatment_responses.notes: No response — mechanism X not involved.

diagnostic_limitations.limitation: Describe why standard measurements systematically underestimate this condition in this patient (e.g., ceiling effects, missing biomarkers, self-limiting behaviour masking symptoms).

additional_context.label: Optional extra context label
additional_context.text: Any other clinical observation not captured above.

clinical._events_note: Ordered list of clinical events. type: infection | reinfection | diagnosis | medication_start | medication_stop | relapse | hospitalization | surgery | symptom_onset | remission | vaccination | other. PRIMARY source is ~/.config/kyoro/clinical_events.json (managed via scripts/utils/manage/personal/manage_clinical_events.py) — cfg.events merges that file with the inline list below, external file wins on (name, date) collisions. The inline list here is only a fallback/example; if you maintain clinical_events.json, code MUST read cfg.events, never this key directly (cfg._cfg['clinical']['events']) — that silently sees only the (usually empty) inline fallback, never the real history.
clinical._events_biography_note: SYNTHETIC EXAMPLE — replace with your own history. Goal: complete medical biography from birth to today, not just current conditions. The more complete the timeline, the better the system detects baseline shifts, turning points, and causal patterns. Include infections (even resolved ones), vaccinations, surgeries, hospitalisations, all diagnoses (acute + chronic), long-term medications (start + stop), relapses/remissions, travel to endemic regions. Go back as far as memory or records allow.

clinical._legacy_note: event_date1/2 and infection_date are derived automatically from events[]. Only set these if you do not use events[].
clinical._afes_note: AFES (Atrial Fibrillation Evidence Score) Geräte-Klassifizierung. exclude_coarse_hr_devices listet device_ids, deren HR-Stream zu grob ist (Smart-Recording-Mittelung), z.B. älteren Garmin-Modellen mit 120s-Recording. sleep_device_priority bestimmt die Reihenfolge für Sleep-Session-Erkennung. wrist_hr_devices wird automatisch aus device_registry abgeleitet (sensor_type in {optical_wrist, optical_wrist_gps, ring}), kann hier überschrieben werden. ecg_quality_devices: Brustgurt-/ECG-Geräte für Pre-AF-Trainings-Filter; wird automatisch aus device_registry (sensor_type == 'chest_strap') abgeleitet.
clinical._sleep_source_priority_note: Quellen-Priorität (session.source-Werte, beste zuerst) für analyse_bp_sleep.py's Auswahl der besten Schlaf-Session pro Nacht bei mehreren überlappenden Quellen. Leer = keine Priorisierung (erste gefundene Session gewinnt). Beispielwerte je nach eigenem Geräte-Setup: z.B. ['oura_app', 'sleep_cycle', 'garmin_connect', 'polar_connect'].
clinical._polar_wrist_date_reassignments_note: Nur relevant, falls scripts/migrations/fix_polar_wrist_device_attribution.py gebraucht wird (historische Polar-Wrist-Daten ohne per-entry Geräte-ID, fälschlich einem Platzhalter-device_id zugeordnet). Jeder Eintrag: {new_device_id, date_condition (rohe SQL-Bedingung auf die Spalte 'date')}. Leer = Migration ist No-Op. Beispiel: [{"new_device_id": "polar_m430", "date_condition": "date < '2022-01-01'"}].
clinical._pem_note: PEM Evidence Score (compute_pem.py). Dreistufige Quellen-Hierarchie: 1) Polar RMSSD, 2) Apple Watch SDNN, 3) RHR-Proxy. Alle Thresholds konfigurierbar. AT-Schwellen-Hierarchie fuer den HF-ueber-AT-Trigger-Kanal: 1) HRVT1 (DFA-alpha1-basiert, individuell) 2) falls fehlend UND rhr_baseline_stable=true (Standard): RHR+at_rhr_offset_bpm (Workwell-Faustregel, Standard 15bpm) 3) falls weder HRVT1 noch RHR verfuegbar: at_hr_fraction als Anteil HRmax (Standard 0.60, unbelegter Notfallwert). rhr_baseline_stable auf false setzen, wenn die Ruhe-HF bei dieser Person kein stabiler Bezugswert ist (z.B. dauerhafte statt punktuelle HF-Erhoehung durch orthostatische Instabilitaet) — deaktiviert dann den Kanal komplett fuer Tage ohne HRVT1, statt einen irrefuehrenden bpm-Fallback zu nutzen. at_hr_fraction: aerobler Notfall-Threshold = Anteil HRmax (Standard 0.60), nur relevant wenn auch RHR fehlt. recovery_ratio: Anteil Baseline ab dem HRV/RHR als 'erholt' gilt (Standard 0.90 = 90%). supcomp_ratio für HRV: 1.05 = 5% über Baseline. Für RHR intern 1.03. pem_ratio: Schwelle für PEM-Muster (Standard 0.85 = 15% unter Baseline). ortho_*: von compute_orthostatic_detection.py gelesen (dieselbe clinical.pem-Sektion, kein eigener Config-Block) — ortho_hr_jump_min: Mindest-HF-Sprung in bpm für einen Kandidaten; ortho_ref_window_s / ortho_onset_window_s / ortho_sustain_min_s: Referenz-, Anstiegs- und Mindesthaltedauer-Fenster in Sekunden; ortho_steps_max: max. Schritte im Bestätigungsfenster (Sport-Ausschluss); ortho_min_beats: Mindest-Beat-Anzahl für eine gültige Messung; ortho_artifact_pct_max: max. Artefaktanteil im Fenster; ortho_pulse_ms_floor: Untergrenze für Puls-Rohwerte in ms; ortho_bp_window_min: Zeitfenster für den Blutdruck-Gegencheck in Minuten; ortho_bp_sys_drop_min / ortho_bp_dia_drop_min: Sheldon-2015-Schwellen für systolischen/diastolischen Abfall in mmHg.

_privacy_check_note: forbidden_identifiers: Python identifier fragments that must not appear in source code (e.g. diagnosis names used as variable/constant names). The check script (check_source_privacy.py) reads these at runtime and stays diagnosis-agnostic itself.
_synthesis_panel_note: Multi-model consult panel config for scripts/analysis/manual/analyse_synthesis.py (Config.synthesis_panel). PRIMARY source is ~/.config/kyoro/synthesis_panel.json (no manage_*.py script for it yet — hand-edit the JSON directly, it's a 4-line file). The inline synthesis_panel block below is only a fallback if that external file doesn't exist. Schema: enabled (bool) — turns the multi-model panel on/off, panel disabled falls back to a single _call_llm() with chair_model; members (list of OpenRouter model IDs) — each independently reads the specialist reports category-by-category (own notes, own final opinion, never sees peers mid-process) before the chair sees any of it; chair_model (OpenRouter model ID) — reads raw data only (AI interpretation sections stripped) in its own category rounds, only compares against the members' finished opinions in the final round.
